chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-A'la ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I said to him: 'Who among a man's relatives is obligated upon him to spend on?' He said: 'The two parents, and the child/children, and the wife.'

key_terms.الوالدان: The two parents — both mother and father
key_terms.الولد: The child/children — includes both sons and daughters
key_terms.يلزم: Obligatory/necessitated — a legal term indicating a binding duty (wajib)
key_terms.ينفق: To spend/provide maintenance (nafaqah) — financial support covering food, clothing, shelter

ai.seo_question: Who are the relatives a man must financially support according to Islamic law?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) defines the immediate family members upon whom a man has a legally obligatory duty of financial maintenance (nafaqah). This hadith comes in response to a direct question from Muhammad ibn Muslim, one of the most trusted jurists among the Imam's disciples. The ruling — parents, children, and wife — reflects the core of Islamic family law, where the husband/son is the primary provider. The original audience would have understood this as establishing the minimal legal threshold of obligatory maintenance, distinct from voluntary charity to more distant relatives.

en.hubeali:
Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘
I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Who from his relatives are necessitated upon the man, from the ones he has to spend upon?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The two parents, and the children, and the wife’.
en.sarwar: 3. Sahl ibn Ziyad has narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from ‘Ala’ ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following:
“I asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘Who are one’s dependents for whom providing sustenance is obligatory on him?’ He (the Imam) replied, ‘Such people are one’s parents, children and wife.’”
